Marathon Petroleum stock rose 1.94% today, continuing a strong two-week rally that's up 9% overall. The climb reflects tightening refinery economics: U.S. refineries are running at 96.8% capacity with oil prices at $107 per barrel domestically but $130.80 globally—that spread between domestic and world crude prices expands refiner margins, making it more profitable to process oil into gasoline and diesel. The jump accelerated over the past four days as news of Saudi Arabia releasing additional crude supplies onto the market eased geopolitical disruption fears that had briefly spiked prices upward.

A refiner's core profit engine depends on buying cheap crude and selling expensive fuel. When global oil sits well above U.S. prices (as it does now by $24 per barrel), and refineries are running near full throttle, those profit margins widen considerably. The broader market narrative—that Middle East tensions may be cooling and fresh crude is flowing—removes a overhang that could have constricted supply and benefited refiners selectively.
